newsitem.title: USA: US High Court denies MAXXAM unit timber appeal.
newsitem.headline: US High Court denies MAXXAM unit timber appeal.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court denied Tuesday an appeal by a MAXXAM Inc unit challenging an injunction barring it from logging in an old-growth forest in California because of the marbled murrelet, a seabird that breeds in such forests.
The case stemmed from a lawsuit filed in 1993 by a group called the Environmental Protection Information Center against the unit, Pacific Lumber Co.
Pacific Lumber had proposed in 1990 to conduct a selective harvest of some timber from a 137-acre stand of trees in the Owl Creek forest in southern Humboldt County.
The forest consisted of old-growth redwood and Douglas fir trees. The murrelet has been listed by the federal government as a threatened, not an endangered, species, along the Pacific Coast.
The environmental group charged the proposed logging would result in a "taking" of the murrelet in violation of the federal endangered species law.
After an eight-day trial, a federal judge in California issued a permanent injunction barring Pacific Lumber from harvesting the trees. A U.S. appeals court last year upheld the decision.

Pacific Lumber appealed to the Supreme Court, asking the justices to hear the case and to rule in its favor. But the high court denied the company's appeal without comment or dissent, an action which affects the parties in a particular case but does not create nationwide precedent.
